newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway C. Bank invites offers to manage oil fund.
newsitem.headline: Norway C. Bank invites offers to manage oil fund.

text.p: Norway's central bank, Norges Bank, said on Monday it was inviting Norwegian and foreign management companies to submit offers for the management of the equity portfolio of the Government Petroleum Fund.
Parliament in June endorsed a proposal contained in the revised national budget for part of the petroleum fund to be invested in foreign equities.
Norway is expected to have a budget surplus of more than 57 billion crowns ($7.8 billion) in 1997 because of revenues from the country's booming oil and gas industry.

This surplus is put into the fund -- which is expected to top 100 million crowns at the end of the year -- for investment to secure the future and pension payments for an increasingly aging population. Norges Bank manages the fund based on guidelines issued by the Finance Ministry.
Norges Bank said the invitation for bids would close on August 8. Management of the equity portfolio is due to start in January, 1998.
It said that in the first of two rounds connected with the invitation, bidders should submit plans for the management of index portfolios.

"This must entail that the managers must spread investments over countries and enterprises so that the portfolio achieves a return that is nearly identical to movements in well-defined share indices," the bank said in a statement.
"In order to minimise the risk of deviation from these indices, the managers must spread investments over most or all of the enterprises included in the indices."
A management strategy based on indices was in line with signals given in the government's revised national budget, it said.
The bank will enlist an international consultancy firm to assist in the selection of managers. ($ = 7.278 Norwegian Crowns)
